scope: Proposition B.1 (Normalized cubic approximation) of the manuscript “Universal optimality of the triangular lattice” (preprints/Universal-optimality-of-the-triangular-lattice-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 090 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 50daa477c52b1f3e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let 0 ≤ s < 2, and fix 1 < p < 2 for s = 0, or 1 < p < min(2, 2/s, 3/(s + 1)) for s > 0. Let A1 be the compatible gradient fields in this fixed Lp loc class, with simple locally finite configurations and unit background. Then the limit W(E) = lim η↓0  lim sup R→∞ R−2 Qη(E, R) − κg(η)  exists in R ∪ {+∞} and is bounded below uniformly over A1. Its infimum m is finite. There are integers Rj → ∞ and simple configurations Cj, periodic under 2RjZ2, with 4R2 j points per period cell, whose canonical periodic values satisfy V (Cj) −→ m. The approximating fields may therefore be chosen to be canonical periodic gradients in the same fixed-p class.
